Company:     Preply

DESCRIPTION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
We power people’s progress.
At Preply, we’re all about creating life-changing learning experiences. We help people discover the magic of the perfect tutor, craft a personalised learning journey, and stay motivated to keep growing. Our approach is human-led, tech-enabled - and it’s creating real impact.
We’ve just reached unicorn status with a $150M Series D, accelerating our vision to transform education through human-led, AI-enhanced learning. Today, 100,000+ tutors teach 90+ languages to learners in 180 countries - and we’re only getting started. As a category-defining company, we’re shaping what the future of learning looks like at global scale.
Every Preply lesson sparks change, fuels ambition, and drives progress that matters. Joining Preply means helping define the future of education at global scale, and building something that truly matters for millions of people, every day.
Meet the team!
This role is embedded within either the B2B domain and is part of Preply’s Data Chapter. You will work closely with directors, B2B leaders, and cross-functional partners across finance and product teams, while collaborating with data analysts, data scientists, and analytics engineers to strengthen analytical foundations and business impact.
What you’ll be doing:
Partner with senior stakeholders across Business and Operations to proactively identify where new analyses, metrics, or frameworks can unlock improvements in retention, revenue, and operational efficiency.
Build and own the analytical framework leadership uses to evaluate B2B trade-offs, and define the long-term measurement framework that identifies structural growth levers, not just incremental wins.
Lead high-complexity, end-to-end analytical initiatives — including retention and cohort analyses that answer specific open questions from B2B leadership — uncovering root causes behind revenue retention, LTV, churn, utilization, and cost efficiency, and turning findings into concrete pricing, product, or lifecycle recommendations.
Own impact modeling, scenario analysis, and KPI governance for B2B: resolve conflicting metric definitions across Operations, Finance, Marketing, and Product, maintain a single source of truth, and feed directly into quarterly and annual planning.
Design the experimentation and analytics agenda, what gets tested, how success is measured, and translate results into executive-ready storytelling that aligns stakeholders on goals and trade-offs.
Partner with Directors and VPs to shape B2B strategy, embed analytics into daily decision-making, and mentor senior analysts to raise the analytical bar.
What you need to succeed:
5+ years of experience in analytics roles (ideally in B2B), with demonstrated ownership of KPI frameworks and measurable impact on retention, revenue, or efficiency.
You can point to specific decisions (a pricing change, a resourcing call, a roadmap cut) that happened because of your analysis, and one where your recommendation was rejected, with the judgment to explain why, in hindsight, that was right or wrong.
You've owned a metric or strategic framework other teams were required to use, and resolved a conflict between two teams who each wanted a different definition to win.
Deep understanding of retention and performance metrics (revenue retention, LTV, churn, utilization, cost efficiency), and the ability to build an LTV or cohort model from scratch, not just interpret one someone else built.
Strong, independent SQL, you're the person other analysts send their code to for review; proven ability to lead cross-functional analytical projects end-to-end.
Strong business acumen and stakeholder influence: comfortable saying no to a request that wasn't the right question, clarifying trade-offs in metrics and resourcing, and building forecast or scenario models that leadership uses to defend a bet to their own leadership.
Nice to have:
Background in B2B SaaS, enterprise, or account-based business models; exposure to customer support operations.
Experience building or scaling an analytics function (hiring, tooling, process, KPI frameworks).
Hands-on experience with Looker, Snowflake, Tableau, or Power BI.
Working knowledge of Python for analysis.
Master's or PhD in a quantitative field.
Why you’ll love it at Preply:
An open, collaborative, dynamic and diverse culture;
A generous monthly allowance for lessons on Preply.com, Learning & Development budget and time off for your self-development;
A competitive financial package with equity, leave allowance and health insurance;
Not in Barcelona? We offer an attractive relocation package to join us in our Preply Barcelona Hub
Access to free mental health support platforms;
Access to Gympass-partnered wellness and gym centers throughout Spain to promote and support well-being and physical health;
The opportunity to unlock the potential of learners and tutors through language learning and teaching in 175 countries (and counting!).
Our Principles
Care to change the world - We are passionate about our work and care deeply about its impact to be life changing.
We do it for learners - For both Preply and tutors, learners are why we do what we do. Every day we focus on empowering tutors to deliver an exceptional learning experience.
Keep perfecting - To create an outstanding customer experience, we focus on simplicity, smoothness, and enjoyment, continually perfecting it as every detail matters.
Now is the time - In a fast-paced world, it matters how quickly we act. Now is the time to make great things happen.
Disciplined execution - What makes us disciplined is the excellence in our execution. We set clear goals, focus on what matters, and utilize our resources efficiently.
Dive deep - We leverage business acumen and curiosity to investigate disparities between numbers and stories, unlocking meaningful insights to guide our decisions.
Growth mindset - We proactively seek growth opportunities and believe today's best performance becomes tomorrow's starting point. We humbly embrace feedback and learn from setbacks.
Raise the bar - We raise our performance standards continuously, alongside each new hire and promotion. We build diverse and high-performing teams that can make a real difference.
Challenge, disagree and commit - We value open and candid communication, even when we don’t fully agree. We speak our minds, challenge when necessary, and fully commit to decisions once made.
One Preply - We prioritize collaboration, inclusion, and the success of our team over personal ambitions. Together, we support and celebrate each other's progress.
Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
Preply.com is committed to creating an inclusive environment where people of diverse backgrounds can thrive. We believe that the presence of different opinions and viewpoints is a key ingredient for our success as a multicultural Ed-Tech company. That means that Preply will consider all applications for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age or veteran status.

Senior Forecasting Analyst – Healthcare - Barcelona, Spain

Shaping the evolution of the forecasting processes and methodologies.

Job Description
YOUR MISSION
Rider cost is one of the largest cost lines at Glovo with more than 20 markets with very different economics. Your mission is to own business performance for our largest and most strategic markets, and to make sure the Controlling system behind them holds: that we see risks and opportunities early, that targets get challenged rather than accepted, and that analysis turns into decisions our markets actually execute. You will do this as a senior individual contributor with genuine decision ownership, your job is not to report on performance, but to drive it.
THE JOURNEY
Own rider business performance across our whole 20+ markets. You are the senior counterpart to Country Heads of Operations, Finance and General Managers in our largest markets, challenging their targets, deviations and recovery plans without formal authority .Across the rest of the portfolio, you will steer the overall picture, coaching and stepping in when an issue becomes material, ambiguous or cross-market
Own the 360° view of our rider business KPIs. Cost is the headline, but it is only one dimension. You will own the full performance picture for our rider operations, cost per order and budget delivery alongside utilisation, delivery times, reassignments, supply health and rider experience, and you will be the person who holds the trade-offs between them. A market that hits its cost target by quietly degrading service has not hit its target, and it will be your job to say so. Over time, you become the person in the company who understands this business best.
Find the money, and decide where we look for it. Across a portfolio this size there is always more to investigate than there is capacity to investigate it. You will identify the highest-value risks and opportunities, drawing on experiments, competitor benchmarks and market trends as much as on our own numbers, decide where the organisation spends its analytical effort, and take deep dives all the way through to a decision, always with ROI in mind.
Own material deviations end to end: root cause, accountable owner, recovery plan and follow-through to closure. The goal is that nothing material surfaces for the first time at month close.
Lead the business narrative through our Best Estimate, budget and annual planning cycles, owning the material trade-offs and the senior decisions, and acting as the single reference point for FP&A and Finance leadership rather than one voice among several. Where the returns justify it, you make the case for additional investment to Glovo's executive leadership, controlling the budget is only half the job.
Raise the standard of the Controlling system itself, the standards, definitions, cadence, tooling usage and accountability that determine whether performance management is trustworthy. You will own this globally and set the standard the whole function works to, with a Controlling colleague covering our small and medium markets working with you on a dotted line. There are no direct reports today; as the function grows, there is a credible path to building a team around this scope.
Be the business challenger to our analytics team, who own the forecasting, target-setting engine, models and performance tooling behind many of these decisions. You will need to understand their work well enough to find its weaknesses and make it better, without trying to own it yourself.
Turn performance into decisions for senior leadership, VPs, Glovo leadership, Corporate Strategy and Delivery Hero counterparts, through short, honest, decision-oriented communication.
Qualifications
WHAT YOU WILL BRING TO THE RIDE
Must have
4–7+ years in Business Performance, Controlling, Strategy & Operations, FP&A, Consulting, Marketplace or Operations, including at least one role where you carried real accountability for a budget, a cost line or a market portfolio, not advisory work alone.
A genuine ownership mentality, and comfort operating without direct reports. You find the problem, form your own view, drive the decision, and make sure execution actually follows.
A track record of challenging and influencing stakeholders more senior than you, and getting them to move.
Strong analytical problem solving. You can decompose a performance problem yourself, interrogate someone else's model, and do the maths rather than wait for it.

Description
We are looking for a Business Analyst to join the ACES Data Analytics Team (ADAT) , supporting operational excellence through data-driven dashboarding solutions. In this role, you will be responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining dashboards and underlying data pipelines that provide actionable insights to operations teams. You will work closely with stakeholders across the support function to translate business needs into analytics solutions that drive decision-making and continuous improvement.
Key job responsibilities
i) Design, build, and maintain dashboards and reporting solutions that support operational performance tracking and decision-making
ii) Write and optimize SQL queries to extract, transform, and analyze data from multiple sources
iii) Develop Python scripts for data manipulation, automation, and advanced analytics
iv) Partner with operations stakeholders to understand business requirements and translate them into clear technical specifications
v) Perform root cause analysis on operational metrics, identifying trends, anomalies, and opportunities for improvement
vi) Ensure data accuracy and integrity across all reporting and dashboarding deliverables
vii) Proactively communicate progress, blockers, and risks to stakeholders and leadership
viii) Support KTLO (Keep The Lights On) activities for existing dashboards, including troubleshooting, bug fixes, and enhancements
A day in the life
In particular, Business Analysts will support the team with different types of analyses (from estimating the savings of a new project to calculating the drivers behind the Team’s performance) and work with various stakeholders in Amazon’s Operations. We are looking for profiles with analytics and communication skills, business sense and an excellent knowledge of Excel and the Microsoft Office package.
As a Business Analyst on our team, you own the full cycle from raw data to actionable insight. You write SQL queries to pull operational data from multiple sources, validate it, and transform it into something meaningful. When something looks off in the numbers, you investigate — tracing it back through the pipeline until you find the root cause and flag it to stakeholders before it becomes a problem.
You build and maintain dashboards in QuickSuite that operations teams rely on daily. That means designing layouts, connecting calculated fields, setting up filters, and making sure the right people see the right data at the right level of detail. You iterate on these based on feedback, always looking for ways to make the information clearer and more useful.
You also write Python scripts that automate repetitive work — data validations, scheduled extractions, report generation — things that used to take hours manually and now run in minutes. When a quick ad-hoc analysis comes in from a manager, you use Excel to pivot the data and deliver a clean summary without overengineering it.
Throughout all of this, you share what you find. You communicate insights clearly to stakeholders, walk them through what the data is telling us, and help them make decisions based on evidence rather than assumptions.
About The Team
Our team sits within the ACES organization and provides analytics and dashboarding solutions that support operational functions. We are a medium size, high-impact team focused on delivering clean, scalable, and well-documented analytics that enable data-driven decision-making across operations. We value seamless development practices, proactive communication, and a strong sense of ownership.

DESCRIPTION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
We’re building the future of medical dermatology by focusing on unmet patient needs and giving people the space to think independently, take ownership and make an impact that matters.
Our purpose is simple: to transform patients’ lives by addressing real needs. We work with care, act with courage, keep things simple and focus our innovation where it makes a difference.
Recognised as a Top Employer in Spain since 2008 and in Germany since 2025, we continue to invest in an environment where people can grow and move forward.
If you care differently, you belong here.
MISSION
Reporting to the VP of Center of Excellence (CoE), the Global Market Insights Director defines and leads Almirall’s global market insights capability. The role ensures the generation of robust, forward-looking and actionable insights that inform brand, portfolio, launch and commercial decision-making across franchises, regions and market companies.
The Director integrates primary and secondary market research, competitive intelligence, forecasting, performance analytics and emerging data sources into one coherent business view. Acting as a trusted strategic advisor, the role converts evidence into clear choices, implications and recommendations, enabling leaders to move from “what happened?” to “why did it happen?”, “what is likely to happen?” and “what should we do next?”.
The role owns functional standards, governance, talent, partners and investment prioritisation for GMI, while promoting close collaboration with Franchises, Regions, Finance, Commercial Operations, Customer Experience, Marketing & Launch Excellence, Market Access, Medical Affairs and other enabling functions. All activities must be conducted in line with applicable laws, industry codes and Almirall policies, with appropriate protection of confidential, personal and competitively sensitive information.
Core Responsabilities
Set the GMI vision and strategy. Define a clear, enterprise-wide insights ambition, operating model, priorities and capability roadmap aligned with Almirall’s business and portfolio strategy.
Lead the Global Market Insights organisation. Allocate resources across franchises, brands and priority business questions; clarify accountabilities; and ensure timely, high-quality delivery across cross-franchise and asset-specific work.
Serve as a trusted strategic advisor. Partner with senior commercial, franchise, regional and functional leaders; frame the decisions that matter; challenge assumptions constructively; and bring an independent, evidence-based point of view.
Build an integrated insights ecosystem. Connect customer, patient, market, competitor, sales, access and internal performance signals into a single narrative that identifies opportunities, risks, drivers and implications.
Govern global market research. Set standards for research planning, methodology, sampling, questionnaire design, synthesis and communication; oversee high-value qualitative and quantitative studies; and ensure that the voice of the customer informs strategy.
Lead competitive and market intelligence. Establish an ethical and compliant intelligence cycle that monitors market evolution, competitor strategies, scientific and commercial developments, and emerging disruptors; translate signals into scenarios and early-warning recommendations.
Own forecasting excellence. Govern global forecasting frameworks, assumptions, scenarios and documentation across assets and markets; integrate market, epidemiology, access, competitive and performance perspectives; and improve transparency, consistency and decision usefulness.
Drive performance insight and business optimisation. Monitor sales, market share, customer and execution indicators; distinguish signal from noise; identify root causes; and recommend specific actions to accelerate growth, improve launch readiness and optimise investment.
Strengthen portfolio and launch decisions. Provide insight leadership across lifecycle stages, including market opportunity assessment, indication and asset prioritisation, target product profile testing, demand and uptake scenarios, launch readiness, and post-launch learning agendas.
Advance analytics, data and AI-enabled insight generation. Promote fit-for-purpose use of advanced analytics, automation and artificial intelligence; partner on data quality and governance; and ensure that innovation remains business-led, transparent, responsible and scalable.
Create decision-focused reporting and storytelling. Establish concise dashboards, executive narratives and structured performance forums that communicate not only findings, but also implications, choices, risks and recommended actions.
Lead external partners and GMI investment. Select and manage research, data and analytics partners; set clear quality expectations; prioritise spend against strategic value; ensure procurement and compliance requirements; and build internal capability where it creates sustainable advantage.
Develop talent and functional excellence. Coach, empower and retain a diverse, high-performing GMI team; build business acumen, consultative influence, methodological expertise and digital fluency; create succession and development plans; and foster accountability and continuous learning.
Embed global-local collaboration. Create effective feedback loops with regions and market companies, balancing global consistency with local relevance, and enabling reuse of evidence, methods and learning across the organisation.
Champion change and continuous improvement. Challenge the status quo, simplify ways of working and anticipate future capability needs while balancing urgent business requirements with long-term value creation.
Education & Experience
Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Economics, Life Sciences, Data Science, Statistics, Engineering or a related field.
Minimum 10–12 years of progressive experience in market insights, market research, forecasting, business analytics, competitive intelligence or strategic marketing within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology or closely related healthcare sector.
Proven experience leading a global or regional insights function and developing people in an international, matrix organisation.
Demonstrated mastery of primary and secondary research, forecasting, competitive intelligence, performance analytics and insight synthesis, with the judgement to select the right approach for the business question.
Strong pharmaceutical business acumen, including brand strategy, launches, lifecycle management, customer and patient dynamics, market access and the global-local operating model.
Experience influencing senior leaders and cross-functional teams through clear recommendations, constructive challenge and compelling executive communication.
Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, external partners and significant research or data investments with a focus on quality, impact and efficiency.
Fluent English, written and spoken, with the ability to operate effectively across cultures and geographies.

MBA, MSc, PhD or other relevant advanced degree.
Experience in both affiliate or regional roles and a global commercial organisation.
Experience in dermatology, immunology, specialty care and/or biologics, including launch and lifecycle insight needs (Desirable).

To deliver our medicines to patients we need to develop evidence for health technology assessment (HTA) bodies and payers around the world. This requires expertise in HTA science where we can translate data into evidence to support decision-making across the lifecycle of our medicines. In Europe, the start of the Joint Clinical Assessment (JCA) will require innovative solutions in demonstrating our comparative effectiveness through direct and indirect analyses, and consideration of how we pull through such evidence into economic value at the national level.
With our expanding oncology portfolio and increasing use of HTA around the globe, we are looking for a passionate and talented individual with experience and pragmatic expertise in health economic modelling to join our global oncology HTA and Modelling Science (HMS) team to support HTA strategy and submission work. Job Description
YOUR MISSION
Rider cost is one of the largest cost lines at Glovo with more than 20 markets with very different economics. Your mission is to own business performance for our largest and most strategic markets, and to make sure the Controlling system behind them holds: that we see risks and opportunities early, that targets get challenged rather than accepted, and that analysis turns into decisions our markets actually execute. You will do this as a senior individual contributor with genuine decision ownership, your job is not to report on performance, but to drive it.
THE JOURNEY
Own rider business performance across our whole 20+ markets. You are the senior counterpart to Country Heads of Operations, Finance and General Managers in our largest markets, challenging their targets, deviations and recovery plans without formal authority .Across the rest of the portfolio, you will steer the overall picture, coaching and stepping in when an issue becomes material, ambiguous or cross-market
Own the 360° view of our rider business KPIs. Cost is the headline, but it is only one dimension. You will own the full performance picture for our rider operations, cost per order and budget delivery alongside utilisation, delivery times, reassignments, supply health and rider experience, and you will be the person who holds the trade-offs between them. A market that hits its cost target by quietly degrading service has not hit its target, and it will be your job to say so. Over time, you become the person in the company who understands this business best.
Find the money, and decide where we look for it. Across a portfolio this size there is always more to investigate than there is capacity to investigate it. You will identify the highest-value risks and opportunities, drawing on experiments, competitor benchmarks and market trends as much as on our own numbers, decide where the organisation spends its analytical effort, and take deep dives all the way through to a decision, always with ROI in mind.
Own material deviations end to end: root cause, accountable owner, recovery plan and follow-through to closure. The goal is that nothing material surfaces for the first time at month close.
Lead the business narrative through our Best Estimate, budget and annual planning cycles, owning the material trade-offs and the senior decisions, and acting as the single reference point for FP&A and Finance leadership rather than one voice among several. Where the returns justify it, you make the case for additional investment to Glovo's executive leadership, controlling the budget is only half the job.
Raise the standard of the Controlling system itself, the standards, definitions, cadence, tooling usage and accountability that determine whether performance management is trustworthy. You will own this globally and set the standard the whole function works to, with a Controlling colleague covering our small and medium markets working with you on a dotted line. There are no direct reports today; as the function grows, there is a credible path to building a team around this scope.
Be the business challenger to our analytics team, who own the forecasting, target-setting engine, models and performance tooling behind many of these decisions. You will need to understand their work well enough to find its weaknesses and make it better, without trying to own it yourself.
Turn performance into decisions for senior leadership, VPs, Glovo leadership, Corporate Strategy and Delivery Hero counterparts, through short, honest, decision-oriented communication.
Qualifications
WHAT YOU WILL BRING TO THE RIDE
Must have
4–7+ years in Business Performance, Controlling, Strategy & Operations, FP&A, Consulting, Marketplace or Operations, including at least one role where you carried real accountability for a budget, a cost line or a market portfolio, not advisory work alone.
A genuine ownership mentality, and comfort operating without direct reports. You find the problem, form your own view, drive the decision, and make sure execution actually follows.
A track record of challenging and influencing stakeholders more senior than you, and getting them to move.
Strong analytical problem solving. You can decompose a performance problem yourself, interrogate someone else's model, and do the maths rather than wait for it.
Comfort with ambiguity, and the judgement to tell signal from noise and focus on what is material.
Advanced Excel / Google Sheets, high comfort with complex data, and fluent English.
Clear, direct communication. You lead with the conclusion and you say what you don't know.
Comfort using AI tools to accelerate your own analysis.
Nice to have
SQL or BI tools such as Looker at a confident user level, enough to answer your own first questions.
Financial fluency sufficient to hold your own with FP&A and Finance leadership on budgets, deviations and planning cycles.

Description
Do you want to make the invisible visible, turning complex model outputs into clear, actionable insights that shape how Amazon moves millions of packages?
We are looking for a Business Intelligence Engineer to own the analytics and explainability layer for Fulfillment Optimization systems that transform network-level plans into actionable signals, systems that tell fulfillment centers and trucks exactly how fast packages should flow, how capacity should be allocated, and how volume should be distributed across the network.
In this role, you will take loosely defined questions about model behavior, output quality, and business impact and refine them into analytical solutions that drive your team's decisions. You will design and own pipelines that decompose model outputs into interpretable signals across multiple planning and optimization systems, build dashboards and automated reporting that surface anomalies and inflection points, and develop the metrics that quantify how output shape and quality connect to fulfillment performance, transportation cost, and customer delivery promise. You will trace data lineage from the technical systems generating inputs through model transformation to downstream consumption, ensuring stakeholders understand not just what the numbers say but where they come from. You will work in SQL, Python, and AWS analytics services to deliver efficient, testable, and maintainable solutions that balance speed of delivery with long-term reliability.
What makes this role compelling is the direct line between your analysis and operational decisions. You are not reporting on historical trends. You are building the analytical foundation that tells us whether our models are producing the outcomes we expect and where opportunities exist to improve. You will partner with BIE and analytics teams across the organization to align on shared measurement approaches, connect your insights with broader network-level metrics, and enable self-service access to underlying data so stakeholders can explore without bottlenecks. You will collaborate with research scientists to validate model behavior, with engineering to instrument systems for observability, and with business stakeholders to recommend alternatives and anticipate future needs. If you enjoy refining loosely defined analytical problems, partnering across teams, and building the layer that connects model behavior to business outcomes, this is the role for you.
Key job responsibilities
Design and own explainability frameworks that decompose model outputs across multiple Fulfillment Optimization systems into interpretable, actionable signals for science, engineering, and business stakeholders
Build analytical pipelines and dashboards that monitor output shape and quality, detect anomalies, and quantify the relationship between model behavior and fulfillment performance
Partner with BIE and analytics teams to align on shared metrics, enable self-service data access, and connect optimization insights with network-level reporting
Trace data lineage from source systems through model transformation to downstream consumption, and translate findings into recommendations that inform team prioritization decisions
Basic Qualifications
Experience with data visualization using Tableau, Quicksight, or similar tools
Experience using SQL to pull data from a database or data warehouse and scripting experience (Python) to process data for modeling
Bachelor's degree or above in BI, finance, engineering, statistics, computer science, mathematics, finance or equivalent quantitative field
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with AWS solutions such as EC2, DynamoDB, S3, and Redshift
Knowledge of Microsoft Excel at an advanced level, including: pivot tables, macros, index/match, vlookup, VBA, data links, etc.

Overview
WELCOME TO SITA
At SITA, we keep airports moving, airlines flying smoothly, and borders open. Our technology and communication innovations power the success of the global air travel industry.
You'll find us in 95% of international airports, working closely with over 2,500 transportation and government clients. Each partnership brings unique challenges, and we thrive on delivering fresh solutions and cutting-edge tech to keep operations running like clockwork. We don't just move the world forward-we're proud to be recognized as a
Great Place to Work
® by 79% of our employees and certified in most of our growing locations. Here, we feel empowered, supported, and inspired to grow.
Are you ready to love your job?
The adventure begins right here, with you, at SITA.
PURPOSE
As the trusted partner to the BU CFO for all Business Finance matters, the Senior Finance Business Partner enables financially sound planning and decision making across the partner organization. The role spreads financial acumen, tells clear, data-driven stories that spur action, bridges the gap between finance and operations, and helps shape the decision support tools delivered with Data and Analytics / FP&A.
The role takes a technology-guided, coaching-led approach to partnering, enabling decision makers to act more independently. It interprets data, advises the business and supports long-run performance management, drawing on a deep understanding of SITA's business models and financial drivers to convert analysis into decisions, targets and outcomes. It does not produce reporting; production is owned centrally by Data and Analytics / FP&A.
Support technology and operations cost transparency and investment decisions, project and product, productivity economics and investment business cases across the technology portfolio.
Key Responsibilities
Deepen decision makers’ Business Finance acumen to enable independent decision making:
Provide continuous coaching to decision makers, helping them understand the way Business Finance analyzes a situation and arrives at an insight, and then apply it consistently in their decision-making processes.
Influence decisions through narrative and visuals: Turn Business Finance analysis into a clear, compelling story tied to the decision at hand, to build conviction and move business leaders to act. Draw on the standardized reports and dashboards produced by Data and Analytics / FP&A and BI, or self-serve tailored, decision-specific visuals through tools such as ERP analytics and Copilot, always on the single governed data source. The measure is the quality of the decisions taken, not the volume of analysis produced.
Challenge decision makers’ assumptions (e.g., by teaching them problem analysis or leading them through root-cause exercises of their current obstacles) to reduce bias and introduce finance’s perspective.
Train decision makers on using value-driver trees to connect operational decisions’ effects on optimizing enterprise value creation (e.g., risk mitigation actions, investment prioritization) and assess the financial impacts of decisions.
Assist with improving decision makers' financial data literacy (e.g., through identifying learning programs, storytelling that translates financial data and modeling into business language or shadowing live scenario analysis) to improve decision makers’ understanding of the financial impact and risks associated with different scenarios.
Assess and anticipate decision makers’ needs:
Build strong relationships with executives and business unit leaders to understand their financial needs and challenges and anticipate the most effective support path.
Surface decision makers’ latent needs by actively listening to uncover new opportunities for decision support tools and services, produced by Data and Analytics / FP&A.
Enable rapid improvement in service and support via a continuous feedback loop with all decision makers.
Provide in-depth, highly personalized decision support to executive decision makers:
Seek ways to continuously and proactively guide executives to meet and surpass performance goals.
Monitor leading indicators to identify initiative delivery risks and operational performance gaps, drive action or provide alternative approaches.
Help executives determine where to drive enterprise value or mitigate risk (e.g., through metric prioritization).
Provide direct support to nonexecutive decision makers when appropriate:
Assess inbound support requests from partners to determine prioritization. Determine if the request could be served by an existing decision support tool or if it warrants the creation of a new one.
Identify cost optimization opportunities and assist in planning cost-reduction strategies.
During the budgeting process, engage in budget pressure-testing, providing Business Finance expertise to ensure stakeholders understand potential risks and constraints.
Lead the preparation of comprehensive business cases for investments and product initiatives (internal funding / M&A), aligned to strategy, helping stakeholders set out the benefits, costs and risks to secure funding and approval. Apply an ROI-focused mindset, building solid, realistic, achievable, measurable and stress-tested financial models. Work cross-functionally with pricing, product and transversal teams to gather inputs; present and defend cases at the Investment Board for instance; post-approval, track actual ROI against projected outcomes and drive action plans; and lead integration plans post M&A signature.
Assist in identifying performance issues and provide help in course-correcting
Facilitate the creation of digital decision support tools:
Work with technology teams to ensure that decision support tools provide actionable advice for a variety of operational and strategic decisions.
Be the “voice of the internal customer” in meetings with Data and Analytics / FP&A and technology teams to help design intuitive reports, analyses, and dashboards that meet the needs of nonexecutive decision makers.
Drive partners decision maker adoption of decision support tools:
Identify the appropriate decision support tools for individual stakeholder needs.
Articulate and demonstrate the value of decision support tool utilization for decision makers (e.g., share success stories, use early adopters as change champions) and tailor the message for different audience types.
Advocate for and assist in developing change management strategies to facilitate the adoption of new tools and processes
Translate financial insight into clear business language when embedding it in decision support tools, so that recommendations are intuitive and readily actionable for the decision makers who use them.
Monitor and assess the value of support:
Champion and participate in knowledge-sharing forums for Finance Business Partners and Data and Analytics / FP&A to exchange lessons learned on how to best educate decision makers in Business Finance’s thought processes during decision support.
Assist in defining success criteria for Data and Analytics / FP&A decision support tools and establishing measurable business and technical metrics to actively monitor utilization and quality.

================================================================================
Job ID:      4467965665
Company:     Nuitée
Location:    Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain
Date Posted: 5 days ago

DESCRIPTION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
About the role
Barcelona or Palma
Nuitée is hiring a Flight Analyst to own the financial accuracy of our Flights business.
A single flight booking touches an airline, a GDS, a supplier, Nuitée's own platform, and the customer — each with its own record of what was charged. You'll be the person who makes sure those numbers agree: tracing bookings from the raw PNR and ticketing data through to the supplier invoice and the customer charge, catching mismatches, figuring out why they happened, and making sure Finance always has clean, trustworthy data to work from.
This isn't a traditional accounting role. You'll sit at the intersection of Flights, Finance, Data and Engineering; and as you build real expertise in how flight pricing works, the role will grow from reconciliation into margin analysis and pricing strategy.
Flights is one of Nuitée's fastest-growing pillars: the product, integrations (GDS, low-cost carriers, NDC), and 50+ customers are already in place, and this role exists to make sure the financial controls scale with it. Nuitée has grown significantly since 2022 and raised a $48M Series A led by Accel.
What makes it interesting for you:
Real financial ownership from day one; the numbers you reconcile directly protect revenue and margin
A clear growth path: you start in reconciliation and move into revenue, pricing and margin analysis as you build domain expertise
Cross-functional exposure to Flights Product, Finance and Engineering, not a siloed back-office role
You're building process, not inheriting one; a lot of what's manual today is being automated, and you'll shape how
The kind of problems you'll work on:
Why doesn't this supplier's invoice match what we actually booked?
Is this a one-off pricing error, or a systematic issue running across thousands of bookings?
What's really driving the margin on this route or this supplier, and how do we improve it?
How do we automate reconciliation so it scales without needing more people to do it manually?
This role fits someone who:
Has 3+ years of experience in the airline, flight distribution, OTA, TMC, GDS or related travel industry
Understands how airline bookings and ticketing work; PNRs, tickets, fares, taxes, commissions, GDS processes
Understands airline pricing concepts: published vs. private/net fares, markups, commissions
Has strong SQL skills and is comfortable reconciling large datasets; BigQuery or similar warehouse experience
Has experience with Looker Studio or a similar BI tool, and strong Excel/Google Sheets skills
Has excellent attention to detail; comfortable tracing a discrepancy down to a single booking
Bonus if you've worked with GDS platforms, airline consolidators, or have hands-on experience with airline settlement/reconciliation processes or flight financial accounting.
You will do well here if you genuinely enjoy finding the reason two numbers that should match don't, and you're comfortable moving between a supplier invoice, a SQL query, a PNR and an internal ledger until you understand exactly what happened.
This is less suited to someone who wants a purely accounting-style role with no data work, or who needs the role's scope fixed from day one — this one is expected to expand as you grow into it.
If that resonates, we'd love to hear from you. You can apply with your LinkedIn profile or CV. The interview process is straightforward and typically takes 3 weeks.

•	Aplicar técnicas de estadística y Machine Learning para desarrollar modelos predictivos y generar insights accionables para las diferentes áreas de negocio.
•	Evaluar y validar la precisión y el rendimiento de dichos modelos utilizando técnicas como la validación cruzada, conjuntos de prueba y métricas de desempeño adecuadas.
•	Colaborar con el equipo de MLOps para integrar los modelos desarrollados en un entorno de producción.
•	Trabajar en estrecha colaboración con equipos interdisciplinarios como ingenieros de datos, analistas, expertos en el dominio y equipos de negocio para comprender los requisitos y objetivos del proyecto.
•	Participar en la toma y definición de requisitos, identificando las necesidades de negocio y traduciendo problemas de negocio en casos de uso y soluciones analíticas.
•	Comunicar de manera efectiva los análisis, resultados de los modelos e implicaciones a diferentes audiencias, incluyendo stakeholders no técnicos, a través de informes, presentaciones y visualizaciones comprensibles. El objetivo será facilitar la toma de decisiones basada en datos.
•	Monitorizar el rendimiento de los modelos en producción, realizar mantenimientos periódicos y actualizarlos cuando sea necesario para garantizar su vigencia y precisión.
•	Mantenerse actualizado en técnicas analíticas como machine learning, optimización, deep learning y análisis de texto.
Para ello, ¿qué vas a necesitar?
•	Education: Grado, Máster o Doctorado en Informática, Economía, ADE, Ciencia de Datos o un campo relacionado.
•	Más de 2 años de experiencia en Data Science, con experiencia en almacenamiento de datos, procesos ETL e integración de datos. Se valorará especialmente experiencia trabajando de forma autónoma en proyectos de estadística y Machine Learning.
•	Conocimiento avanzado de SQL: dominio en la escritura y optimización de consultas.
•	Experiencia en desarrollo en entornos AWS, Azure o Google Cloud.
•	Conocimiento profundo del modelado de datos, gobernanza y mejores prácticas de calidad.

•	Experiencia en scripts de Python y familiaridad con bibliotecas y herramientas de Python.
•	Experiencia práctica en técnicas de Machine Learning y estadística aplicada, incluyendo modelos predictivos, regresión, clasificación, clustering y/o series temporales.
•	Se valorará tener conocimientos estadísticos: pruebas de hipótesis, análisis de regresión, distribuciones de probabilidad, etc.

About The Role
Theia Insights builds foundational financial intelligence products, including industry classification, knowledge graphs and factor risk models, for institutional investors. We serve some of the largest asset managers, hedge funds, index providers and sell-side banks. As a quant engineer on the Data Products team you'll build and run the models behind our Thematic Factor Risk Models (TFM): decomposing stock returns into thematic and traditional risk factors, back-testing methodologies and turning research into daily production output alongside our economics team. The Data Products team owns the data that underpins everything we sell. It's a small, senior group that values correctness and reproducibility over volume, and it sits close to the product leads who shape the methodology.
What You'll Do
Develop statistical models of stock price movements and estimate the performance of thematic trends
Construct and back-test factor risk models, decomposing stock returns into thematic and traditional risk factors
Design and validate signal-generation and portfolio-attribution methodologies in collaboration with the economics team
Make research reproducible, so that any published output can be re-run exactly, including after backfills and restatements
Work with the pipelines team to take modelling decisions into daily production
Requirements
Essential
Strong production Python
Factor risk models and portfolio attribution in depth: cross-sectional regression, covariance estimation and shrinkage, and back-tests you'd defend line by line
Point-in-time discipline, look-ahead and survivorship bias, and reconstructing what was knowable on a given date
Statistical modelling and optimisation (statsmodels, cvxpy; PyTorch useful)
Datasets in pandas and Parquet/Arrow, plus an analytical engine such as DuckDB
Nice to have
Quantitative research background, academic or industry
Index construction and classification taxonomies
Working with model-derived inputs, understanding that NLP-generated exposures carry measurement error and revise over time
Task orchestration (Dagster or Airflow) and S3-based data flows
AWS fluency and CI/CD discipline
Benefits
Competitive salary plus share options

JOB #400: Predoctoral Researcher On Financial Inclusion
================================================================================
Job ID:      4459755359
Company:     EMBA La Salle
Location:    Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain
Date Posted: 3 weeks ago
URL:         https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/4459755359/

DESCRIPTION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Predoctoral Researcher on Financial Inclusion
IQS Barcelona invites applications for a Predoctoral Researcher Funding Contract to work on the project "Financial inclusion tools to address the challenges related to accessing financial services".
The position offers a three-year scholarship and full-time employment starting in March ****, covering doctoral tuition and providing a full employment contract within the Business and Territorial Competitiveness, Innovation and Sustainability (CETIS) program at the IQS School of Management, Universitat Ramon Llull, Barcelona, Spain.
Financial Inclusion (FI) is recognized as a crucial instrument for economic advancement.
This project explores barriers to FI and tools to improve access to financial services.
Key obstacles include high service costs, limited branch access, misaligned risk assessments, poor financial education, and weak regulations.
To address these, the project aims to examine innovative solutions such as microfinance, blockchain, and the formal use of remittances.
By focusing on both supply and demand challenges, the project seeks to identify effective Financial Inclusion Tools (FITs) that can combat poverty and marginalization, extending FI benefits to developing, transition, and developed economies.
In this PhD project we will investigate eight FITs: mobile money, non-bank financial distribution, behavioural credit risk, workers' remittances, adapted financial regulation, financial education, microfinance business models, and blockchain technology.
The Research Will Pursue Three Core Objectives
(i) construct and analyze novel indicators of financial inclusion across regions;
(ii) assess the effectiveness of the FITs; and
(iii) generate and propose new FITs to address access challenges.
This highly data-driven, interdisciplinary effort combines finance and economic sciences, employing advanced econometric techniques, experimental research, and a novel panel dataset.
Key Responsibilities
The doctoral researcher, based at IQS School of Management, will conduct core research activities leading to their PhD thesis within the project "Financial inclusion tools to address the challenges related to accessing financial services."
Responsibilities include advanced data processing and analysis, indicator development, and contribution to experimental research components.
The researcher will also actively participate in training activities, research seminars, and collaborative initiatives led by the Sustainability, Economics and Ethics Research Group (SEE).
Light teaching assistance may also be assigned.
Desired Candidate Profile
We invite applications from candidates with a strong academic background and proven interest in financial inclusion and payments, development economics, financial access data analysis, or related fields.
Applicants should hold a Master's degree (MSc) in finance, economics, data science, engineering, or other relevant disciplines in social or applied sciences.
Strong data processing skills, including experience in database management and applied statistics.
Solid methodological background in quantitative analysis for empirical research (e.g., econometrics, panel data, statistical computing).
Experience in statistical programming and data processing using tools such as Excel, Stata, MATLAB, Python, or similar.
Interest in applied research or experimental design (valued but not mandatory).
Selection Process
Prospective candidates are invited to submit a proposal and brief work plan outlining their research interests and how their background and expertise could contribute to the objectives of the project.
Innovative ideas on how to address financial inclusion challenges will be especially valued.
Application Requirements and Submission Deadline

Project Proposal And Work Plan, Which Must Include
Title.
Project summary (maximum 100 words).
Detailed description of the proposed work plan (maximum 2,000 words).

JOB #459: Applied Scientist, SCOT FO - SnT
================================================================================
Job ID:      4466990537
Company:     Amazon Science
Location:    Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain
Date Posted: 1 day ago
URL:         https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/4466990537/

DESCRIPTION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Description
How does Amazon decide which fulfillment center ships your order, which truck carries it, and how to keep promises across hundreds of millions of packages daily? How does it decide how many trucks and how much labor are required to ship orders across the network?
SCOT Fulfillment Optimization (FO) owns the optimization and forecasting science behind these decisions.
We are seeking Applied Scientists to join the FO Science & Tech team in Barcelona (alternatively: Luxembourg or London) with a strong academic background in optimization, machine learning, and/or time-series forecasting.
You Will Design And Build State-of-the-art Machine Learning And Optimization Models That Power Amazon's Fulfillment Decisions At An Unprecedented Scale Across Two Core Scientific Pillars
Large-Scale Optimization and Planning: Designing planning systems for order assignment and resource utilization, while balancing multi-objective cost-speed tradeoffs to enable controllers to steer millions of shipments per hour optimally.
Demand Forecasting & Predictive ML: Developing time-series forecasts for customer demand, incorporating contextual information (weather, sales, order properties), and modeling uncertainty for core planning systems.
Basic Qualifications
PhD in Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field (or equivalent experience)
Strong programming skills (Python preferred; experience with optimization solvers a plus)
Research experience in one or more:
Large-scale mathematical programming (LP, MIP, decomposition methods)
Combinatorial optimization (assignment, scheduling, network flows)
Multi-objective optimization and control
Large-scale time-series forecasting (GenAI models, probabilistic forecasting, uncertainty quantification)
Causal inference (spatiotemporal causal modeling, offline policy evaluation)
Preferred Qualifications
Experience building optimization systems that run in production at scale
Being comfortable with ambiguity and fast iteration cycles
Publications in relevant venues
Key job responsibilities
Design and implement optimization and forecasting models for large-scale fulfillment problems, from order assignment to network flow control. Build research prototypes end-to-end: from problem formulation through scalable implementation to production validation. Analyse complex tradeoffs (cost, speed, capacity, accuracy) and translate findings into actionable recommendations for leadership and operations teams. Collaborate with engineers to bring science solutions into production systems serving millions of customer orders daily.
A day in the life
You formulate an optimization or forecasting problem on a whiteboard with teammates, then prototype it in Python with real data by the afternoon. You run experiments against production-scale datasets, iterate on the model, and present results to stakeholders who will use them to make network decisions next week. Some days you dive deep into solver performance; other days you're explaining a Pareto frontier to an operations leader. You collaborate with large engineering and product teams to bring your solutions into systems serving millions of customers. Alongside fast-turnaround prototypes, you own long-term research bets, the kind that reshape how Amazon's fulfillment network operates at scale. Your work goes live.
About The Team
SCOT Fulfillment Optimization Science & Tech (FO SnT) is the applied research team behind Amazon's fulfillment decision-making systems. We decide how orders get assigned to warehouses, how capacity is allocated across the network, and how cost and speed tradeoffs are managed in real time, at global scale. Our models influence billions of euros in annual operational spend. They protect sites from overload during peak, reduce transportation costs and CO2 emissions, and ensure customers receive their packages when promised. Leadership relies on our science to make investment decisions worth hundreds of millions. We are practitioners of large-scale optimization: MIP formulations, decomposition methods, approximation algorithms, and parallelisation. We use machine learning where it sharpens our decisions, including forecasting, learned heuristics, and multi-armed bandits. We pick the right tool for the problem, not the fashionable one. You will work alongside Senior and Principal scientists, and collaborate with Amazon Scholars and academic partners who bring frontier research into our applied problems. We code our prototypes to be production-ready and collaborate with large engineering teams to ship systems, not papers. Above all, we have fun solving hard real-world problems at real-world speed, failing, learning, and shipping along the way.
Basic Qualifications
PhD, or a Master's degree and experience in CS, CE, ML or related field
Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
Experience in building models for business application
Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and distributed computing, high-performance computing
Preferred Qualifications
Experience using Unix/Linux
